text:
Alex K: Heads up — CI flagged a p95 regression on the release-ci perf job after yesterday's merge (PR #2987). current delta ~18% on short-seq workloads, baseline stable before merge.
Samir P: saw the alert. which change in #2987 looks suspicious?
Alex K: early bisect points at the batching heuristic tweak + kernel selector rule that landed in runtime/kernel_selector.py (commit b3f9c2). seems to prefer grouped-kernel for batch sizes 2-4 now.
perf-ci-bot: [alert] perf/latency p95 increased to 172ms (was 146ms) on integration/short-seq · job: release-ci · build: 5158 · threshold exceeded
Maria S: hmm we also have a KV-cache eviction change in #2971 that touched should_sticky logic for infrequent prefixes. could be causing cache misses and extra KV loads.
Jen L: do we have a repro harness for the short-seq scenario?
Samir P: yes, run ./tools/perf/run_local.sh --profile=short-seq --runs=50 on a pinned commit. I ran it locally across commits in the merge and see the step jump exactly after b3f9c2.
Priya R: if bisect points to kernel_selector, can we make a minimal change to prefer legacy-kernel for seq<=8 until we understand perf implications? that would be a quick rollback without reverting whole PR.
Tomas V: I dug into logs — when grouped-kernel is chosen for short sequences we actually pay extra kernel-launch overhead because batch concat path disables a fast-path. that plus 15% extra KV misses explains the 18% net.
Alex K: plan options: 1) revert kernel_selector change (full revert PR), 2) cherry-pick targeted fix that adds a hard threshold for short sequences, 3) patch should_sticky in KV cache to reduce evictions.
Maria S: 3) alone won't fix the kernel overhead. 2) seems safest for quick rollback. we can backport to release branch v1.8.x.
Jen L: agree. create a minimal PR that adds `if seq_len <= 8: prefer_legacy=True` with a feature-flag guard and link to perf results. then run canary.
Samir P: I'll open the cherry-pick PR onto the release branch and include perf artifacts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3012 (draft).
Alex K: tagging @release-team — we need a backport to v1.8.2 and a patch verification job. deploy-bot please create a canary image.
deploy-bot: creating canary image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:canary-perf-1850 -> done. image digest sha256:abcd1234
perf-ci-bot: queued canary perf run on infra-canary-us-east · run id 78902
Priya R: Samir, also include a small unit test to assert kernel choice for seq_len 1..8 so we don't regress again.
Samir P: added tests in PR 3012 + linked the bisect log. running CI now.
Jen L: once CI passes, can we run the canary against the internal staging workload for 2 hours and compare p95 and cache hit rate? need numbers to approve backport.
Tomas V: I'll set up the staging run and capture KV hit-rate metrics (+token counts). expecting hit-rate to go from ~82% back to ~94% with this change.
Maria S: also add rollback instructions in the PR description with exact git commands for the release engineer:
```
# revert full PR
git checkout release/v1.8.x
git revert -m 1 <merge-commit-sha>
# or cherry-pick fix
git cherry-pick <fix-commit-sha>
```
Alex K: good. timeline: Samir opens PR now, get CI + unit tests green within 1 hour, canary perf run results in ~2 hours, release-team decides to backport if p95 drops to baseline within 5% and KV hit-rate recovers.
Samir P: CI passed on the cherry-pick branch. canary run started (run id 78902). attaching perf summary when done.
perf-ci-bot: canary run 78902 completed · p95=148ms · KV-hit=93.7% · regression mitigated ✅
Jen L: excellent. release-team, can we proceed with the backport PR to v1.8.2 and schedule a hotfix release?
release-team: scheduling hotfix window at 22:00 UTC.
Maria S: once backport PR is merged I'll kick off the release pipeline and monitor the canary in prod for first 30 mins. if anything odd, we'll do an immediate revert.
Alex K: thanks all. postmortem follow-up: add a perf-check gating for kernel_selector changes on the CI job that runs small-seq perf profiles. ticket: ENG-4123.
Priya R: noted, I'll own ENG-4123 and draft the gating job config.
Tomas V: will prepare a short write-up on why grouped-kernel hurts short-seq and propose longer-term heuristics.
Alex K: copy that. closing thread once backport is merged. :thumbsup:
